Thanks Tessa — recap looks right. A few clarifications from our side before the deep-dive:

Questions for the tech session:
- Can you confirm separation of admin activity logs vs API request logs? We need distinct streams and schema examples.
- What export formats do you support? Prefer newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) or compressed CSV.
- Do you support push-based exports to our S3 bucket with bucket-owner-full-control and server-side encryption with our KMS?
- For immutability: do you provide WORM-like guarantees, tamper-evident manifests, or signed hashing of exported bundles? If not, will Redwood include immutable audit manifest generation so we can lock objects on our side?
- Retention: configurable retention per-log type? Can we set different retention windows for admin vs API?

Also, please include your SOC 2 status and the date of the most recent report — Medicorp requires the report or an attestation for onboarding.

I completed the RFI with a couple of initial comments (see attached). If you can provide a sample export (sanitized) and a short doc describing the export handshake and auth (presigned vs push), that will help our security team.

Hi Samantha / Tom — Rishi from the platform team here. Short technical answers and what we'll demo in the deep-dive: 

Quick answers:
- Streams: we emit two canonical log streams: admin_activity (user changes, role grants, console actions) and api_requests (inference request metadata, model id, tokens, status). Each stream has a documented schema; we'll attach sample NDJSON.
- Formats: NDJSON (preferred) and gzip-compressed CSV are supported. Our sample export will be NDJSON with one JSON object per line.
- Delivery: push to customer S3 is supported (we operate a push agent that can write objects with server-side encryption and preferred ACLs), or we can provide presigned PUT URLs for you to pull. We support KMS-keyed encryption for both sides.
- Immutability: Redwood can produce a signed manifest for each export (SHA256 list + timestamp + Redwoods signature). We do not modify exported bundles after generation. For a WORM guarantee, recommended pattern: Redwood pushes export bundles, and Medicorp applies S3 Object Lock Governance/Compliance mode and verifies signed manifest hashes. We will include signed manifests in the export bundle.
- Retention: retention is configurable per-stream at the org level; we can set different windows for admin_activity vs api_requests and enforce minimums in Dedicated deployments.

What we'll demo in the 30-min tech deep-dive:
- Walk-through of sample NDJSON export (schema mapping).
- Export handshake: presigned vs push, auth flow, and error/retry guarantees.
- Signed manifest generation and verification example.
- Quick Q&A about retention and role-based access to logs.

I attached a tiny sanitized sample export and a short manifest example.

Rgds,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
